findings.title: post-edit-diagnostics: spawnSync('tsc') cannot resolve the .cmd shim on Windows — the entire TS/JS diagnostics path is silently dead on the primary platform, and the early return also skips the bus 'edited' write for every TS/JS edit

findings.observe_how: ls of C:/Users/david.hayes/AppData/Roaming/npm and .claude/hooks/node_modules/.bin shows only tsc (sh), tsc.cmd, tsc.ps1 — no tsc.exe. Node spawnSync on win32 resolves only .exe, so result.error (ENOENT) fires and the hook prints '{}' BEFORE recordBusFilesInPlay (line 255). The project's own C.1 platform contract documents this exact trap; user CLAUDE.md still claims '*.ts/*.tsx edits trigger automatic tsc --noEmit diagnostics' — a decision-driving false claim. Fix per windows-platform.md finding #1: invoke the real JS entrypoint (node <pkg>/typescript/bin/tsc) or cmd.exe /c tsc.cmd with array args, and hoist recordBusFilesInPlay above the early returns.

findings.title: tree-invalidate: root-level depth heuristic is separator-dependent and wrong for absolute paths — forward-slash Windows paths (depth=1 when split on path.sep '\\') make EVERY .ts/.py edit 'significant', backslash paths make the branch dead

evidence.quote: // Any new TypeScript/Python module file at root level

causal_links: amplifies D2e-06 (more invalidation writes -> more chances to race/corrupt the tree file)
findings.observe_how: tool_input.file_path is always absolute. On Windows path.sep='\\': a 'C:/Users/...' forward-slash path splits into 1 segment (depth 1 <= 4 -> always significant -> tree marked stale on every TS/Py edit anywhere); a 'C:\\Users\\...' path is always >4 segments (branch never fires, contradicting the 'root level' intent). Compute depth relative to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR after normalizing separators.
findings.telemetry: _invalidated_at churn rate in .claude/knowledge-tree.json vs actual significant edits

findings.title: tree-invalidate: non-atomic writeFileSync rewrite of knowledge-tree.json (read-modify-write, no temp+rename, no lock) — plausible producer of the documented 'Empty tree file (0 bytes)' failure mode under crash/concurrent sessions

findings.title: pageindex-watch: trailing-edge debounce never fires — the final batch of indexed-doc edits is never reindexed until some LATER indexed edit arrives (possibly days later or from another project), leaving PageIndex stale by design

evidence.quote:
const elapsed = now - pending.timestamp;
  if (elapsed >= DEBOUNCE_MS) {

findings.observe_how: First edit creates pending (elapsed=0 < 2000ms) and exits; the trigger only runs on a SUBSEQUENT indexed-file edit. A session that edits ROADMAP.md once and stops never reindexes it. The 2s window also means nearly every second edit triggers a full background `uv run ... batch_index` spawn (uv startup is the known 13-17s class, SEED-08), so the debounce neither batches well nor flushes reliably. A detached setTimeout-flush child or SessionEnd flush closes the hole.
findings.telemetry: compare mtime of indexed docs vs pageindex_* rows; count of orphaned pageindex-pending.json entries

findings.title: Bus writer inconsistency: post-edit-diagnostics records 'edited' files as RAW ABSOLUTE paths with no existence/containment/noise validation, while bus-tool-populator stores validated project-relative paths — and the edited-role write is skipped whenever diagnostics early-return (daemon unavailable, tsc missing)

evidence.quote: addFileInPlay(b, { path: filePath, role: 'edited', turn_added: b.current_turn ?? 0 });

if (isNoise(rel)) return null;
  return rel;

causal_links: caused-by D2e-02 (tsc early return is the dominant skip path on Windows)
findings.observe_how: Single-writer discipline itself is CLEAN (only post-edit-diagnostics, bus-tool-populator, bus-session-populator call mutateBus; caps enforced in addFileInPlay AND at the coerceBus read chokepoint). But the two PostToolUse writers disagree on path canon: 'edited' rows are absolute (C:\\... or C:/...), unfiltered (node_modules/out-of-project edits recorded), so (path,role) dedup and any future path-keyed consumer sees two formats. Today's B.3 reader only takes basenames (bus-focus.ts basenameNoExt), which masks the inconsistency. Also: recordBusFilesInPlay is placed AFTER the unavailable/tsc early returns, so the comment 'runs before the early-return' only holds for the clean-file case. Route the edited path through toRecordablePath and hoist the call.

findings.title: architecture-stats-sync: non-unref'd 1s safety-net setTimeout in readStdin keeps the hook process alive ~1 second on EVERY Bash PostToolUse — a fixed latency floor added to every Bash call in the session
findings.observe_how: The timer is never cleared or unref'd, so even after stdin 'end' resolves and main() prints its output, the live timer holds the event loop and the process cannot exit until ~1000ms have elapsed. Claude Code waits for hook exit, so every Bash tool call registered to this hook pays ~1s. One-line fix: `setTimeout(...).unref()` or clearTimeout on 'end'.
findings.telemetry: wall-time of the architecture-stats-sync hook per Bash call (should be ~50ms Node startup, observed ~1s+)

findings.title: import-validator: module-path verification compares forward-slash expectedModule against TLDR daemon result paths — on Windows (backslash daemon paths) the includes() check can never match, turning every resolvable local import into a false 'imported from X but defined in Y' warning

evidence.quote: warnings.push(`${symbol}: imported from ${imp.module} but defined in ${actualFile}`);

findings.observe_how: INFERRED because the TLDR daemon's result.file separator format was not traced. If daemon paths use '\\' (native Windows), 'scripts/core/recall' never substring-matches 'scripts\\core\\recall_learnings.py' and the hook injects a wrong-location warning for a CORRECT import — a false claim in context (would be S1 if confirmed). Verify with one daemon search on Windows; fix is normalizing check.location separators before includes(). Also note the substring heuristic ('def <symbol>' FTS) false-positives on same-named local symbols shadowing stdlib imports.
findings.telemetry: rate of '[Import check]' injections on imports that actually resolve (pyright clean)

coverage_manifest: git-auto-commit.ts — ISSUES: S1 shell-interpolated git commit/check-ignore commands (D2e-01); S3 sibling-prefix isInClaudeDir match (D2e-12). Debounce, fail-open, and tracked-only gating otherwise sound; note `git add -A` batches ALL ~/.claude changes by design.

tree-invalidate.ts — ISSUES: S2 separator-dependent depth heuristic mis-classifies every absolute path (D2e-05); S2 non-atomic knowledge-tree.json rewrite matching the documented 0-byte failure mode (D2e-06). Stale-marker-instead-of-delete design itself is good.

pageindex-watch.ts — ISSUES: S2 trailing-edge debounce never flushes the last batch (D2e-07); S3 global cross-session pending file race (D2e-13). Detached uv spawn with windowsHide and env PYTHONPATH is correct.

import-validator.ts — ISSUE: S2 INFERRED separator mismatch in module-path verification likely yields false 'defined in Y' warnings on Windows (D2e-10); telemetry tracked only when warnings found (biased counter, not separately filed). Daemon-fail-soft behavior is correct.

telemetry-tracker.ts — ISSUE: S2 awaited 2s-bounded Braintrust emit per Skill call with a contradictory 'Fire-and-forget' comment + dead eslint-disable (D2e-04, SEED-16 class). detectToolError swap and tool_response_keys instrumentation are sound; jsonl append unbounded but out of scope here.
mcp-activity-tracker.ts — CLEAN. Minimal catch-all with instant non-MCP exit; only cost is Node process startup per tool call (platform-wide pattern, not specific to this hook).
vercel-deploy-context.ts — CLEAN. Regex push detection, existsSync gate, fail-open, VITEST guard all correct; only theoretical false positive is 'git push' inside a quoted string after ;/&&.

post-edit-diagnostics.ts — ISSUES: S1 spawnSync('tsc') dead on Windows + early-return skips the bus edited write (D2e-02); S2 whole-project blocking tsc per edit once fixed (D2e-03); S2 writer-inconsistency raw-absolute unvalidated bus paths + write placement after early returns (D2e-08). Bus write goes through mutateBus (single-writer OK); Python daemon path is correct.
web-lookup-advisor.ts — MINOR: S3 failure-heuristic false positives (D2e-14). Site map + suggestion construction fine.

sentry-deploy-release.ts — CLEAN. Deploy regex, three-manifest Sentry detection, fail-open and perf targets hold; does not check deploy success before injecting (same class as D2e-15, not separately filed under the S3 cap).
linear-branch-context.ts — CLEAN. Pure regex extract + string build, <1ms paths as advertised; LINEAR_WORKSPACE default documented in code.

architecture-stats-sync.ts — ISSUES: S2 non-unref'd 1s stdin safety-net timer delays every Bash PostToolUse exit (D2e-09); S3 fires off HEAD even when the commit failed (D2e-15). Watched-path regex and detached spawn-to-logfile are correct; no Braintrust emit by design (audit invariant respected).

bus-tool-populator.ts — CLEAN. Exemplary writer: realpath containment + isNoise filter + project-relative canon, GREP_HIT_CAP=8/200-line scan bound, ambient role for grep vs load-bearing for Read per design, mutateBus-only (single-writer), fail-open, '{}' always emitted.

shared/context-bus.ts (verification target, not assigned-for-findings) — single-writer discipline VERIFIED: mutateBus callers in src/ are exactly post-edit-diagnostics, bus-tool-populator, bus-session-populator (all hooks); caps enforced at BOTH write helpers (LOAD_BEARING_CAP/FOCUS_SYMBOLS_CAP/RECENT_FINDINGS_CAP/OPEN_THREADS_CAP=50, ambient 30% + floor 3) and the coerceBus read chokepoint; 200ms lock cap with logged (never silent) drops; traversal-validated bus id with containment assert.
notes: Dimension D2e: 13 PostToolUse hooks reviewed at SHA 86b8f60 (working tree). Method: full Read of all 13 sources plus shared/context-bus.ts and shared/bus-focus.ts (bus contract verification), registration grep across repo .claude/settings.json / active ~/.claude/settings.json, and on-disk verification that no tsc.exe exists (npm global + hooks node_modules/.bin contain only tsc/tsc.cmd/tsc.ps1). No tests executed; no files written. Bus verdict: single-writer discipline and caps are correctly implemented and enforced at both write and read chokepoints; the real bus problems are writer-side (D2e-02/D2e-08: the edited role silently missing for TS/JS on Windows, and un-canonicalized absolute paths from post-edit-diagnostics). Highest-leverage fixes: D2e-02 (restores both TS diagnostics and bus edited-role on the primary platform; the project's own windows-platform.md already prescribes the spawn pattern) and D2e-09 (one-line .unref() removes ~1s from every Bash call). D2e-10 needs a 5-minute daemon-path-format probe to confirm or kill; if confirmed it upgrades to S1 (false claims injected into context). settings.json.template does not exist at repo root (wizard templates live elsewhere) — template-gap accounting stays with SEED-15.
